newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Howard says no horror budget.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Howard says no horror budget.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday that Australians should not fear a horror budget in May.
When asked by reporters if they should, Howard said: "No."
He said the estimating error made by the Treasury and the Australian Taxation Office which resulted in a revision upwards of fiscal 1996/97 budget expectations was regrettable.
"It's regrettable but we've revealed the situation and we're setting about fixing it," he told reporters.
Treasurer Peter Costello on Tuesday announced a revised forecast for the 1996/97 (June 30) underlying budget deficit of A$8.49 billion, compared with the A$5.65 billion forecast in the August budget.
Further budget tightening would therefore be needed if the government were to balance its books by 1998/99, as planned, Costello said on Tuesday.
Asked whether he would call an early election if an outstanding budget bill was again rejected by the upper house, the Senate, Howard said he preferred that parliaments run their full term.
"I don't deal in empty threats. I want to serve three years," he said.
The August budget announced A$7.2 billion in savings, of which the government lost about A$400 million when the Senate refused to pass the necessary legislation last year.

The government has previously said that A$200 million was irredeemably lost but that it would put the other A$200 million, depending mostly on a bill to restrict migrant's initial social security entitlements, back before the Senate again this year.
